text: chemical elements that are not metals
rule: 2 = article about one element whose text identifies it as a nonmetal, noble gas or halogen; 1 = article about a compound, group or material centred on nonmetals, an element whose text also describes metal-like behavior (for example astatine) or is a metalloid, or an element article whose text does not state its class; 0 = metal, person, general periodic table article, or unrelated

text: diseases that do not spread from person to person
rule: 2 = article about a disease or its pathogen whose text states there is no, or no documented or shown, person-to-person (human-to-human) transmission; 1 = text says such transmission is rare or limited; 0 = otherwise, including articles not about a disease or pathogen

2 = article about a spacecraft, class of spacecraft, probe, lander or test flight whose text explicitly calls it uncrewed or unmanned; 1 = robotic probe, orbiter or lander with no explicit crew statement, or a launch-vehicle article whose text says it launched uncrewed payloads; 0 = crewed craft, articles covering both crewed and uncrewed programs, people, equipment, or incidental mentions of uncrewed flights

2 = article about an Atlas rocket (any variant, or an Atlas-derived system such as Atlas-Agena), an Atlas missile, an Atlas engine or stage, or a Mercury-Atlas flight; 1 = article centred on a person or object tied to a Mercury-Atlas flight, or a rocket design built around an Atlas booster; 0 = other senses of atlas, spacecraft launched on Atlas, or any passing mention of Atlas

2 = article about a published atlas (geographic, world, historical, road or thematic, such as bird or linguistic atlases) or about the history of the atlas as a book; 1 = article about a digital or software atlas, or about cartography or a map collection that discusses atlases without being about one; 0 = rocket, mythology, star-catalogue mention, or any passing mention of an atlas

2 = article about an epidemic, pandemic or outbreak that occurred at least partly between 1801 and 1900, shown by a date or '19th century' in the text; 1 = article whose main subject is a concept, response or history tied to 19th-century epidemics (for example a medical theory or an international conference); 0 = other, including epidemics that began after 1900 and passing mentions

2 = article about a cholera pandemic whose start year, after 1860, is stated in the text; 1 = article about a cholera outbreak after 1860 that is not called a pandemic, or a history article covering such periods; 0 = pandemics that started in 1860 or earlier, or other
2 = article whose main subject is the Mariner 4 mission; 1 = article that gives more than a one-sentence mention of the Mariner 4 flyby; 0 = other Mariner probes, or a one-sentence mention
